title: against all odds
summary: Hailey Jonas was a small girl for her age, and always said the wrong thing.
content:
Hailey Jonas was a small girl for her age, and always said the wrong thing. She was a bit different, though everyone else made sure that she never forgot that she would never fit in.

She usually sat by herself, not many wanted to be with a freak like her, and so she spent the lunch outside on a bench. Her mother had made a salad, though Hailey didn´t feel like eating today. She didn´t feel like doing anything at all, actually. And so she kept on watching the other kids around her play and have fun as they always had.

Not including her.

Hailey had always been kept out, but it was only recently that she had seen that it wasn´t only her, the other kids made fun of. It was at least three other people that she had seen been bullying, and she had also seen both younger and older kids that had been haggard too.

It was sad, Hailey thought. That someone could to such thing to another person just cause they wasn´t the same. As she looked at all the people, it wasn´t so hard for her to see that it wasn´t only her, who sat by themselves, hanging with they shoulders and head.

As school went by and finally rang for the last time, Hailey hurried to get out first. She knew that if she were late, the other kids would stand outside, waiting for her. That´s why she ran out and didn´t stop until she was far enough that she was safe to the day.

Of course, it wasn´t that easy to get away, and it wasn´t long after that the kids came after her, walking just some meters behind her; laughing. Hailey felt her body tense as she heard them laughed, but for once they didn´t laughed at her. Or so, they didn´t yelled things at her and then made it quiet obvious that she was the joke.

Instead they started to do something that Hailey thought was much worse. “We aren´t far from the woods, are we know?” one of them said, hinting to something Hailey didn´t think would happen ever again after the first time that had ended so badly.

“No, it´s just around the corner.”

Hailey got problem breathing. If they were going to hunt her into the woods again, she didn´t know what to do anymore. The first time she had got lost and it felt like she had been in there for days. Her father hadn´t found her before it was dark and she had long ago lost all hope about ever returning.

If they were going to hunt her again, she wasn´t sure she would make it. Not as far to the woods, not as far to home. She hadn´t thought they would actually hit her, even though she had seen them hit other, bigger kids. She had heard the name “knucklehead” been used on one of them, and that had scared the crap out of her.

“You´re Hailey, right?”

She jumped as the tall, black guy walked up beside her. She nearly got panic as she thought that he was one of the boys behind her, that he might be the one they called knucklehead. All thoughts went into each other and she was almost ready to start crying and begging!

But then she heard that the voices behind her had stopped. It was quiet; and that was never a good sign.

“Duane,” one of them called behind them. “What are you doing with the freak? Haven´t you enough trouble as it is, being a alien?” They all started laughing at that; Hail was ready to run. Maybe the woods would be safer after all.

“Ignore them,” the kid whispered toward Hailey. He didn´t look at her, and that she was glad for. All blood had drained form her face, her hands was shaking and the cold sweat was seeping through her cloth. She was so scared that she almost started weeping, but not quiet. “Just walk.”

“Are you Duane?” Hailey managed to ask. Her voice was a little shaken, but it was steadier then she would have thought. She actually thought it would come out of a sob, but it seemed like she could still be a little calm.

The boy nodded, and Hailey let herself look at him out of the corner of her eyes. His skin was dark, though not as dark as the night. His hair was cut short, and had the darkest black colour she had ever seen. He was almost a head taller then her, and a lot broader. She couldn´t see his eyes clearly from the said, but they looked grey.

They kept going, turned the corner and waited. It had to come, was all Hailey thought. They would scream and start running after them, they always did. As they just kept going and Hailey could see the next corner not far ahead, she started finally relaxing. She had never been so glad to walk beside anyone as beside Duane in that moment.

But as every happy moment in Hailey life, someone had to destroy it. And that happen when they came around the second corner – when someone punched Duane right in the jaw.

Hailey screamed before she could stop herself. She was so shocked that she could do nothing but stare as the two boys started to fight. Where he had come form, she didn´t know and didn´t really care. All that was in her head was the bloody face of Duane that she got a glimpse of.

“Stop,” she whispered, unable to drag her eyes away from the two struggling boys. Now the other boys stood beside her, cheering on the other boy they called knucklehead. Hail felt so could she was almost sure that se was in process of dyeing. “Please, stop.”

“Is this you´re new friend?” One of the boys said as he crushed Hailey´s face between his thumb and index finger. His hand covered nearly her whole lower face. Hailey felt her teeth’s imprint in her cheeks, soon the taste of blood. Tears were pouring down her cheeks, yet all she felt was cold and angry.

She was still afraid – so very afraid – though as she saw the boys cheering their friend to crush the black guys face, she understood that it didn´t matter if she was sad, happy, scared of even angry – these boys would never stop this unfairness.

“I asked you something, Dane!” The boy that crushed Hailey´s face slowly yelled. “I think we might do her after you. Then you can watch as we turn her pretty face into a bloody mask!”

It was over Hailey´s understanding ability, to get any sense out of the boys smirk. If he was pleased for giving her pain, he was doing a terrific job! So Hailey did what she did best.

“Are you kicking him because he´s black?” she asked. “Do you not like me because I´m smarter then you?” The boys grip loosen for a moment as he stared at her, not sure if he really had heard her talk. “You do know that this is illegal, so if any get know of this, you can get thrown to jail or even get some kind of pay back by professionals?”

“What the hell are you talking about?” the boy shouted as he pushed Hailey into the wall behind her. Hailey felt the wall press into her back, scrubbing against her fragile skin. Was it going to draw blood? She didn´t think so, not if it he didn’t push her in it again. It did hurt, but she felt vaguely numb, as if it didn´t matter. Hailey was anyway sure they both were going to die.

“Who are going to tell?” one of the other boys laughed, enjoying all that was going on. Hailey started to worry about Duane again. He had tried to help her when he knew what they were going to do with her. It wasn´t fair, not fair at all, that he was being beaten because of that. Maybe that was why Hailey didn´t stop talking?

“You would have gotten away with it if you had attacked us before this corner,” Hail said and looked up as much as she could. “Everything is on tape now. You will be known for racism and hoarsen, and for beating us both to blood.” She tried to shrug, though she didn´t made it while she was pressed up against the wall.

“Crap,” one of the boys said, finally getting that this was worse then bad.

Hail was shock of some sort. She wasn´t sure what she really had did; some part of her still believed that they were going to drag them both into the ally or woods to kill them. It wasn´t likely that they would to that, not that things had been so very ´likely’ for Hailey the past few years.

Then as fast as they had come, as fast they disappeared. The boys and knucklehead ran for their life as they tried to figure a way out of their mess. Still in shock, Hail stood up against the wall for a whiled as she thought about what just happened. Her moth and shoulder´s were stilling burning with faint pain and she still could taste blood, but other then that she felt fine.

“Cameras?” Duane asked as he got up and spited blood out of his mouth. His face was really a bloody mess; he had a black eye, his lip was swollen and his cheekbone had a bad fling. He had blood at his t-shirt too, though he seemed to be just fine. Hailey guessed it could have ended more badly then this.

“They haven´t worked since the day of dawn,” Hailey said, she felt happy again. A faint happiness that she thought she never would feel. Not after so much had gone wrong.

“How did you come up with that?” he asked. He rolled his tongue over his teeth to check if everyone was there. After spitting some more at the ground, he seemed to be pleased of not breaking any teeth´s or bones. Hailey was glad for that too.

“I didn´t,” she declaimed. “I … well, I guess I sort of did, but … I don´t know. Why did you help me?” Instead of trying to figure out how she had come up with the camera idea, she asked a question in repeat, hoping that he might just ignore that she didn´t know what she had did.

In respond, he shrugged and limped round sometimes to try his legs. With some help from Hail, they made it out of the ally they almost had been in, and started to walk. They didn´t say much at they way, though both of them smiled stupidly.
